psi-po.d: Family of objectives \( \max_\pi \mathbb E[\Psi(p^*(y\succ y'))]-\tau\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|\pi_{\text{ref}}) \), with \(y'\) drawn from the data policy. With Ψ = logit it recovers RLHF and DPO; with Ψ = identity it gives IPO.

preferencia-deterministica.d: A pair in which the preferred response wins 100% of the time (\(p=1\)). In DPO it demands an infinite margin for any β, nullifying the KL. With a single label per pair, every pair in the dataset looks deterministic.

teoria-do-prospecto.d: Kahneman and Tversky's decision model: people evaluate outcomes relative to a reference point, are concave in gains, convex in losses and loss-averse. The basis of KTO.

funcao-de-valor.d: \( v(z)=(z-z_0)^\alpha \) for gains and \( -\lambda(z_0-z)^\alpha \) for losses, with medians \(\alpha\approx0.88\) and \(\lambda\approx2.25\) (Tversky and Kahneman, 1992). KTO replaces it with a logistic.

aversao-a-perda.d: Losing an amount hurts more than gaining the same amount pleases: in the value function, \(\lambda>1\) (≈ 2.25 at the measured median). In KTO it becomes the weights \(\lambda_D\) and \(\lambda_U\).

halo.d: Class of losses defined in the KTO paper: the human value of an implicit reward measured against a reference point. DPO and PPO-Clip are HALOs; conditional SFT and SLiC are not.

ponto-de-referencia-kto.d: Estimate of the KL between policy and reference, computed on mismatched pairs within the microbatch, \( \max(0, \text{mean of }\log\frac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_{\text{ref}}}) \), with no gradient. It sets where KTO's logistic saturates.

feedback-binario.d: A single label per response, good or bad (desirable/undesirable), with no comparison pair. It is KTO's format and what production logs (like/dislike) usually provide.

normalizacao-por-comprimento.d: Dividing a response's log-prob (or log-ratio) by its number of tokens. It removes the penalty the sum imposes on long responses and their dominance of the gradient. Used by SimPO, ORPO, normalized DPO (Tülu 3) and TRL's IPO.

margem-alvo.d: In SimPO, how much the preferred response's reward must exceed the rejected one's: \( \sigma(r_w-r_l-\gamma) \). Usually given as \(\gamma/\beta\) (0.5 is a good starting point).

ln-dpo.d: DPO with each log-ratio divided by the response's length, \( -\log\sigma(\frac{\beta}{|y_w|}h_w-\frac{\beta}{|y_l|}h_l) \). It keeps the reference. It was the best in Tülu 3 (β = 5); in TRL it is loss_type "sigmoid_norm".

orpo.d: Combines SFT and preference in a single stage, with no reference: \( \mathcal L_{\text{SFT}}+\lambda\,(-\log\sigma(\log\frac{\text{odds}(y_w)}{\text{odds}(y_l)})) \), with per-token mean probabilities.

razao-de-chances.d: \( \text{odds}=P/(1-P) \). The odds ratio compares two responses by odds instead of probabilities; in ORPO it gives a softer contrast than the probability ratio.

cpo.d: DPO with a uniform reference (the reference terms vanish) plus an NLL on the preferred responses. It uses summed log-probs, so it is length-sensitive.

r-dpo.d: Length-regularized DPO (Park et al., 2024): \( -\log\sigma(\beta\Delta h+\alpha(|y_w|-|y_l|)) \), derived from an RL objective with an \(\alpha|y|\) penalty. It reduces verbosity.

beta-dpo.d: DPO with β adjusted per batch by the mean discrepancy of the implicit rewards: easy pairs call for a larger β, close pairs call for a smaller β (Wu et al., 2024).

dpop.d: DPO with a penalty \( \lambda\max(0,\log\frac{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_w)}{\pi_\theta(y_w)}) \) inside the logit: it forbids the preferred response from dropping below the reference (Pal et al., 2024; β = 0.3, λ = 50).
